Eventown theorem (∣A∣≤2⌊n/2⌋)

Words: 50
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
If every member of a set family on [n] and every distinct pairwise intersection has even size, its characteristic vectors span a self-orthogonal binary subspace. The standard dot product is nondegenerate, so W⊆W⊥ implies 2dimW≤n. Thus the set family has at most 2⌊n/2⌋ members. All unions of ⌊n/2⌋ disjoint pairs of points attain this bound.

Oddtown theorem (∣A∣≤n)

Words: 60
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
If all members of a set family on [n] have odd size and all distinct pairwise intersections have even size, its characteristic vectors over the finite field F2​ are linearly independent. Their pairwise dot products are zero, and each vector has dot product one with itself. Taking the dot product of a linear combination with each vector makes every coefficient vanish, so there are at most n vectors. The set family of all singleton sets attains this bound.

Separating set system (∀i=j ∃A: i∈A, j∈/A)

Words: 82
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
A set family on a finite set separates ordered pairs if each ordered pair of distinct points has a member containing the first point and omitting the second. If its members are A1​,…,Am​, assign each point the characteristic vector of its incidences, or equivalently Ti​={a:i∈Aa​}. Separation in both directions says precisely that the Ti​ form an antichain in the Boolean lattice on m coordinates. Thus the Sperner theorem gives n≤(⌊m/2⌋m​). Conversely, any antichain of n distinct subsets of [m] supplies such a set family by transposing its incidence table.

Large family avoiding a high intersection

Words: 56
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
If a forbidden intersection size exceeds n/2, every subset of size at most ⌊n/2⌋ avoids it, including on self-intersection. This set family contains at least half the Boolean lattice. Consequently a fixed exponential bound cn with c<2 cannot hold uniformly as n grows. Forbidden-intersection estimates below the middle rank therefore cannot simply be extrapolated to high intersections.

Forbidden-intersection density increment ([a,b]↦[a−1,b])

Words: 201 Articles: 1
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
For two set families forbidding all cross-intersections in [a,b], split into absent and present coordinate sections. The section pairs (F1​,G1​), (F0​,G0​∪G1​), and (F1​,G0​∩G1​) forbid, respectively, [a−1,b−1], [a,b], and [a−1,b] in one fewer dimension. For 0<δ≤1/10, either one of the first two pairs, allowing exchange of the set family names, increases the density product by at least 1+δ, or the third widens the interval and retains at least 1−δ−2δ2 of that product. This converts a single forbidden intersection into a long forbidden interval while recording every density gain and loss.

Quantitative forbidden-intersection bound by widening (ρ≤max{e−gℓ+D2n/4,e−gn+(2g+h)ℓ})

Words: 101
Forbidden-intersection density increment OurBigBook.com
Let two set families on n coordinates forbid cross-intersection size ℓ, and let ρ be their density product. For 0<δ≤1/10, put g=log(1+δ), h=−log(1−δ−2δ2), and D=g+h. Repeated forbidden-intersection density increments terminate when one endpoint of the forbidden interval reaches zero or the remaining dimension. In the first case, if v steps widened the interval, the cross-intersection bound from cube separation gives logρ≤−gℓ+Dv−v2/n≤−gℓ+D2n/4. In the second case, at least n−ℓ steps occurred and at most ℓ widened, giving logρ≤−gn+(2g+h)ℓ. For a single set family take the square of its density. Choosing δ=1/50 proves ∣A∣≤1.999n for forbidden intersections n/4 and ⌊n/8⌋, with small dimensions handled directly.

Effective ground-set parameter of a hereditary uniform layer (∣Fm​∣=(mxm​​))

Words: 124 Articles: 1
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
For a nonempty degree-m layer of a down-set in an N-element Boolean lattice, the unique real number xm​≥m with ∣Fm​∣=(mxm​​) measures an effective number of available coordinates. The Lovász shadow bound and ∂Fm+1​⊆Fm​ imply xm+1​≤xm​ whenever the later layer is nonempty. It is a real parameter, not the actual size of the set family's support.

Shadow ratio for a hereditary set family (pm+1​/pm​≤(xm​−m)/(N−m))

Words: 68
Effective ground-set parameter of a hereditary uniform layer OurBigBook.com
For a down-set on N coordinates, let pm​=∣Fm​∣/(mN​). For 1≤m<N with pm​>0, the effective ground-set parameter of a hereditary uniform layer gives the displayed ratio bound. Iteration is valid up to the first empty layer. In particular, whenever 2m≤N, p2m​≤pm2​; if the later layer is empty this conclusion is immediate. Ratios with pm​=0 are undefined and must be replaced by the assertion that all later layers are empty.

Coordinate shifts of a set family (Cij​F)

Words: 287 Articles: 3
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
For distinct coordinates i,j, replace a member containing j but not i by its partner with j exchanged for i, provided that partner is absent. This set family operation preserves cardinality. Repeating shifts with i<j terminates because every change decreases ∑A∈F​∑a∈A​a. Its effect on shadows is described by coordinate-shift shadow containment.

Downward coordinate compression

Words: 160 Articles: 1
Coordinate shifts of a set family OurBigBook.com
In a set family, replace a set containing i by its deletion of i only when that deletion is absent. This preserves cardinality and cannot increase maximum pairwise Hamming distance. If a new set and a retained set gave a larger distance, the retained set's deletion would already have been present; that deletion and the original uncompressed set would give the same distance. Repeated downward compressions yield a down-set.

Two cube edges in every direction force many vertices (∣F∣≥⌈3n/2⌉+1)

Words: 93
Downward coordinate compression OurBigBook.com
For a family in the n-dimensional Boolean lattice, the loss of trace cardinality on deleting coordinate i equals the number of pairs S,S∪{i} both in the family. If every direction has at least two such edges, downward coordinate compression preserves that property. The resulting down-set contains the empty set and all n singletons. Each coordinate must also occur in a two-element member. Those pairs cover all n coordinates and number at least ⌈n/2⌉, giving the bound. For n≥2, the empty set, all singletons and a minimum collection of pairs covering every coordinate attain it.

Coordinate-shift shadow containment (∂Cij​F⊆Cij​∂F)

Words: 75
Coordinate shifts of a set family OurBigBook.com
For a uniform set family, the lower shadow of its shifted set family is contained in the shifted lower shadow. Check the witness in the four patterns of membership in coordinates i,j. A surviving shadow member containing only j must have both old shadow partners; a member containing only i needs either old partner. Taking complements exchanges Cij​ with Cji​ and gives the same containment for the upper shadow. Thus coordinate shifts of a set family cannot increase either shadow or their disjoint union, the external vertex boundary of a uniform set family.

Constant-intersection family bound (∣F∣≤n(λ>0))

Words: 164 Articles: 2
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
If distinct members of a set family on [n] have intersection size λ, then its size is at most n for λ>0, and at most n+1 for λ=0, assuming n≥1. In the positive case, use the Gram matrix of the characteristic vectors of sets; a member of size λ is handled by disjoint remainders. In the zero case nonempty members are disjoint.

Constant t-wise intersection dichotomy (m≤k+t−2)

Words: 105 Articles: 1
Constant-intersection family bound OurBigBook.com
Let m≥t≥3 distinct sets have every t-fold intersection of size λ. Either all contain a common set of size λ, or m≤k+t−2, where k is the minimum size of a (t−2)-fold intersection. Fix such a minimum intersection and restrict the remaining sets to it. Equal traces give the common set; distinct traces satisfy the constant-intersection family bound. The qualification m≥t excludes vacuous counterexamples.

Complement-of-singleton extremizers

Words: 36
Constant t-wise intersection dichotomy OurBigBook.com
The sets Ai​=[m]∖{i} have every t-fold intersection of size m−t and every (t−2)-fold intersection of size m−t+2. For m≥t+1, their common intersection is empty and they attain m=k+t−2 in the constant t-wise intersection dichotomy.

Elementary set shift (Sij​)

Words: 122 Articles: 2
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
For i<j, replace a member A containing j but not i by (A∖{j})∪{i} only when the replacement is absent. An elementary set shift preserves family size and the intersecting family property. The inclusion ∂(Sij​F)⊆Sij​(∂F) shows that it cannot increase the lower shadow.

Shifted set family

Words: 82 Articles: 1
Elementary set shift OurBigBook.com
A set family is shifted if every elementary set shift leaves it unchanged. For a uniform set family, this is equivalent to downward closure under componentwise comparison of the increasing lists of its elements. Repeated elementary set shifts terminate at a shifted set family.

Ballot reflection injection

Words: 50
Shifted set family OurBigBook.com
For a member of a shifted set family that is an intersecting family, find the first prefix with more selected than unselected positions. Reflect membership in that prefix. The result has one fewer element and lies in the lower shadow; the first prefix with more unselected positions gives the inverse. This injection proves the intersecting shadow lemma.

Odd cross-intersection bound (∣A∣∣B∣≤2n+1)

Words: 41
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
Appending a coordinate one to each indicator vector changes every odd cross-intersection dot product into an even one in F2n+1​. The argument for the even cross-intersection bound then gives the displayed bound. It is a valid bound without a claim that it is sharp.

Even cross-intersection bound (∣A∣∣B∣≤2n)

Words: 37
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
If every cross-intersection of two set families on [n] has even size, the spans of their indicator vectors are orthogonal in F2n​. The orthogonal complement over the binary field dimension formula bounds the sum of their dimensions by n, giving the displayed cardinality bound.

Weakly intersecting family in a product alphabet (S(x)={i:xi​>1})

Words: 45
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
Here two words must both have symbols greater than one in some common coordinate, without requiring the symbols to agree. Their supports S(x) therefore form an intersecting family. The fibre of a support of size r contains (k−1)r words, relating this problem to a weighted set family problem.

Bollobas set-pairs inequality (∑i​(∣Ai​∣∣Ai​∣+∣Bi​∣​)−1≤1)

Words: 57
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
For disjoint pairs Ai​,Bi​ such that Ai​∩Bj​=∅ whenever i=j, the displayed sum is at most one. In a uniformly random permutation, the events that all of Ai​ precedes all of Bi​ are disjoint events, and their probabilities are the summands. Taking Bi​ to be the complement of the members Ai​ of an antichain recovers the LYM inequality.

Separating family of disjoint set pairs

Words: 108 Articles: 1
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
A family (Ai​,Bi​)i=1m​ of pairs of disjoint subsets of a finite set separates its points if each two distinct points lie on opposite sides of at least one pair. Empty sides are allowed by this definition. Let d(x) count pairs containing x. Associate to x the subcube of {0,1}m fixing coordinate i to zero on Ai​ and one on Bi​. Separation makes these subcubes disjoint and yields the disjoint subcube packing inequality.

Disjoint subcube packing inequality

Words: 37
Separating family of disjoint set pairs OurBigBook.com
Pairwise disjoint subcubes of {0,1}m fixing d1​,…,dn​ coordinates satisfy ∑x=1n​2−dx​≤1. By Jensen inequality, their average codimension is at least log2​n. Consequently a separating family of disjoint set pairs of total incidence at most λmn, with λ>0, has m≥⌈log2​n/λ⌉.

Symmetric chain decomposition of a Boolean lattice

Words: 169 Articles: 3
Extremal set theory OurBigBook.com
A symmetric chain in the Boolean lattice P([n]) contains one set of each size from r through n−r. A symmetric chain decomposition partitions the Boolean lattice into such chains.

Symmetric chain in a Boolean lattice

Words: 29
Symmetric chain decomposition of a Boolean lattice OurBigBook.com
A symmetric chain contains one subset of each size from k to n−k, nested by inclusion. Its endpoint ranks sum to n. A symmetric chain decomposition of a Boolean lattice partitions all subsets into such chains.

Adjacent-level matching in a Boolean lattice

Words: 62
Symmetric chain decomposition of a Boolean lattice OurBigBook.com
For 1≤i≤n/2, the inclusion graph between ranks i−1 and i of P([n]) has a matching saturating rank i−1. Indeed, each lower vertex has degree n−i+1, each upper vertex has degree i, and edge counting gives
(n−i+1)∣A∣≤i∣N(A)∣
(1)
for every family A in the lower rank. This verifies the condition of the Hall marriage theorem.

The least number of chains partitioning P([n]) is the size of its largest rank:
(⌊n/2⌋n​).
(2)

For equal-size subsets A and B of an ordered ground set, A precedes B in lexicographic order when the smallest element of their symmetric difference belongs to A.

Iterated lower shadow (∂jF)

Words: 98 Articles: 1
Lower shadow OurBigBook.com
Repeatedly take the lower shadow of a uniform set family. After j steps the result consists of all subsets of its members whose size is j smaller. Iterating the Kruskal-Katona theorem shows that colexicographic initial segments minimize every iterated lower shadow.
Clique counting from iterated shadows (∂r−2C⊆E(G))
Words: 68
Iterated lower shadow OurBigBook.com
For the uniform set family of vertex sets of r-cliques, its (r−2)-fold lower shadow consists of graph edges. Repeated use of the Kruskal-Katona theorem bounds clique count from edge count. Sixteen four-cliques have at least twenty-three triples in their shadow and at least eighteen edges in their second shadow, by the expansions 16=(46​)+(33​) and 23=(36​)+(23​). Hence a graph with fifteen edges has at most fifteen four-cliques, attained by the complete graph on six vertices.

Nonisomorphic colex shadow minimizers
Words: 73
Kruskal-Katona theorem OurBigBook.com
Minimum-shadow families need not be unique up to permutation. Four edges of a four-cycle and the first four pairs in colexicographic order both have four vertices in their lower shadow, but the latter graph has a triangle. For triples, the six sets consisting of two points from {1,2,3} and one from {4,5} have a nine-pair shadow. The initial six colex triples also have shadow size nine, but their point degrees are 5,4,4,3,2 instead of 4,4,4,3,3.
Lovász shadow bound (∣F∣=(rx​) ⟹ ∣∂F∣≥(r−1x​))
Words: 130
Kruskal-Katona theorem OurBigBook.com
For a nonempty r-uniform set family, define x>r−1 by ∣F∣=(rx​) using real binomial coefficients. Then its lower shadow has at least (r−1x​) members. This continuous estimate is often easier to use than the exact integer expansion in the Kruskal-Katona theorem.
A short proof uses coordinate shifts of a set family. In a fully left-shifted set family split at coordinate one into F0​ and F1​, deleting one in the present section. The shifting property implies ∂F0​⊆F1​, and the total lower shadow has size ∣F1​∣+∣∂F1​∣. Induct on uniformity and, at fixed uniformity, on set family size. If ∣F1​∣<(r−1x−1​), the Pascal's identity and the size mathematical induction force ∣∂F0​∣>(r−1x−1​), a contradiction. The uniformity mathematical induction applied to F1​, followed by the Pascal's identity, proves the estimate. Integer x is sharp for the full r-level on x coordinates.
Colexicographic section compression (Cicolex​)
Words: 44
Kruskal-Katona theorem OurBigBook.com
Split a uniform set family into the section avoiding a coordinate and the section containing it, with that coordinate removed. Replace each section by a colexicographic initial segment of the same size. Induction on the ground-set size, and nesting of initial segments, show that this operation cannot enlarge the lower shadow.
